feature: A line of text counts as an element
summary: Size mode now reads a heading or a text label as one element: hover it for its width and height, click to keep both. A caliper drawn across a label keeps its number off the words, the way it already keeps off buttons.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Flags are on by default. Open Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/Fixtures/settings-pane-2x.png (the settings pane the earlier audits used).

try.do: Press I for the Measure tool, then press I until the pill reads Size.
Hover the General heading. It outlines as one element with its width and height beside it.
Click it. Two calipers land, 78 px wide and 17 px tall, and one Undo removes both.
Press I again for Size and hover the Launch at login label. The label outlines, not the row.
Press ] once. The pick grows to the row, 624 by 44. Press [ to come back to the label.
Click the label. Its width and height land with both numbers off the letters.
Switch to Distance and click on the two ends of Copy to clipboard, then click below to place the number. It sits under the label, not on the word.
Back in Size, hover the Save Changes button's own words. The button is the pick, not its label.

evaluate: A text line measures its ink, cap top to descender bottom. Is that the number you want for a heading, or do you expect the line box a design tool would quote?
Over a row label the pick is the label and one ] away is the row. Does that feel right, or should the row come first with [ to reach the label?
The words inside a button stay the button. Do you ever want the button's label on its own, and if so is [ the way you would reach for it?
The label's width number lands above its right end with a leader, because the next row sits below. Would you rather it sat on the divider band under the label?
rough: Half points are rounded away: Launch at login is 90.5 by 12.5 points of ink and reads 90 px by 12 px. The formatter has done this for every caliper since the start; text just lands on halves more often.
The width readout of a row label goes above the label with a leader line whenever the next row is close beneath, which is every settings row. Filed as a follow-up.
Text on a photo or a gradient is out of scope: the line reader needs one flat background behind the words and stays quiet otherwise.
The mock's Size mode only ever showed bordered controls; treating a text line as a first-class element is a departure from it, taken because redliners measure text as often as buttons.
